title: NASA Human Research Program
author: NASA Human Research Program
description: Official NASA overview of human health risks, including bone and muscle changes, sleep disruption, and radiation effects during exploration missions.
content: NASA's Human Research Program investigates the health challenges facing astronauts in space, including bone and muscle loss, sleep and circadian disruption, and radiation exposure. These studies guide countermeasures and mission planning.

title: Bone and Muscle Loss in Space
author: NASA Mission Pages
description: Official NASA explanation of microgravity-related changes in bone density and skeletal muscle during spaceflight.
content: Microgravity affects bone remodeling and muscle function, creating risks for astronauts during long-duration missions. NASA documents these structural and physiological changes as part of human research and countermeasure development.

title: Sleep and Circadian Rhythm Research
author: NASA Human Research Program
description: Official NASA topic area covering sleep, circadian rhythms, and behavioral health in orbital missions.
content: Astronaut sleep can be affected by mission schedules, light-dark cycles, confinement, and operational demands. NASA studies these factors as part of crew health and performance protection.

title: Space Radiation and Human Health
author: NASA Space Radiation Analysis Group
description: Official NASA discussion of ionizing radiation exposure in space and its relevance to astronaut health and mission design.
content: Radiation exposure is a major concern for long-duration missions beyond low-Earth orbit. NASA monitors radiation risks and evaluates shielding, medical countermeasures, and operational limits.

title: Microgravity Effects on Human Physiology
author: NASA Human Research Program
description: Official NASA overview of the physiological impact of microgravity on the human body, including musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, and vestibular systems.
content: Extended exposure to microgravity can change cardiovascular function, musculoskeletal health, balance, and fluid distribution. NASA uses these findings to shape mission planning and mitigation strategies.
